claim: A tailer holds the tail of the rope with 33 N while the capstan pulls 5 kN
law: Capstan (Euler-Eytelwein) equation T_load / T_tail = exp(mu theta): four turns, mu 0.20 polyester on painted steel

claim: Four people at the bars give the 5 kN pull with 114 N each
law: Moment balance at the head: M = T (r + bush friction) shared over two bar ends 754 mm from the axis; sustained push per person for short bouts 150 N

claim: Four people can keep up the 1.5 m/min stroke rate
law: Power each = pull x rope speed / 4 = 5,000 N x 0.025 m/s / 4; sustained hand power 75 W per person

claim: A quarter-turn stroke takes in 101 mm of rope
law: Arc length = r x angle, 64.2 mm centre radius, 90 degrees

claim: The 6 mm S275 shear pin, from a bar certified at 410 to 480 MPa ultimate strength, releases below the 8 kN design tension
law: Single shear of a mild steel pin, tau = 0.6 x Rm, torque to rope tension at the head. EN 10025-2 allows 410 to 560 MPa for S275 bar of 3 to 100 mm; at 560 MPa the release would be 8300 N, above 8 kN, so the bar is bought with a mill certificate at 480 MPa or less and three pins per batch are release-tested (HPL-DDR-006); 5 % test scatter
closed_by: HPL-CAL-001 A4; release tests on each pin batch at TRL 4

claim: The same pin does not release below the 5 kN the capstan must pull, even at the bottom of its spread
law: As S5 at the bottom of the certified range (410 MPa) and minus 5 % test scatter
closed_by: HPL-CAL-001 A4; release tests on each pin batch at TRL 4

claim: The rope keeps its factor of 4.5 on break at the top of the pin's release range
law: 14 mm polyester double braid, 40 kN minimum break, 90 % through an eye splice, over the upper release tension (HPL-DDR-001 item 5 sets 4.5)

claim: A 14 mm polyester double braid with at least 40 kN minimum breaking load can be bought
law: Maker's data: Marlow D/Braid PES 14 mm, minimum break load 5,570 kg (about 54.6 kN) (shop.marlowropes.com, checked 2026-11-03); one other maker's article quotes about 4,700 kg (about 46 kN) for 14 mm polyester rope (iropes.com, checked 2026-11-03). Both exceed 40 kN

claim: The 114.3 mm drum and the 60.3 mm hold-down roller do not cut the rope's strength
law: Fibre rope strength and life fall as the bend ratio D/d falls; usual guidance asks for about 8 or more where the rope wraps a sheave or drum. Drum 8.2, roller 4.3 (the rope wraps the roller by only about 15 degrees). The guidance was not checked against a source
check: Drum 8.2, roller 4.3: confirm the figure with the rope supplier
closed_by: Rope supplier's bend-ratio data at TRL 4

claim: The 60.3 x 5.0 post stays below 0.6 of S355 yield at the 8 kN design tension
law: Bending of the post at the centre member from the rope pull; yield S355 355 MPa (EN 10025-2)

claim: One holding pawl takes the full design tension without crushing its tooth
law: Bearing stress on the 12 x 6 mm tooth face at 8 kN (one pawl taking it all); limit 0.6 x S275 yield 275 MPa

claim: The probe reaches 2.5 m in stiffer debris with two people
law: Push needed = cone resistance x tip area + sleeve friction x perimeter x depth (cone 1.0 MPa, sleeve 3 kPa, estimates; no published data for slide debris); two people push 650 N
closed_by: HPL-CAL-001 B1s; test heap at TRL 4

claim: The 16 x 2.0 probe tube does not buckle under one person's push (half of two people's 650 N) at the full 3.07 m free length
law: Euler buckling, pinned ends, E 210 GPa, free length 3.07 m (worst case, start of a push); one person pushes while more than 1.5 m is above the debris, two below that, where the critical load is 2026 N
closed_by: HPL-CAL-001 B2; probe trials at TRL 4

claim: A kneeling searcher on a crawl board sinks less than 50 mm on very loose debris
law: Bearing pressure over the board divided by a subgrade modulus of 0.10 MN/m3 (low side, estimate; no sourced value for slide debris); the load is shared over an assumed 0.8 m length of board
check: 44 mm against 50 mm, resting on an estimated modulus
closed_by: HPL-CAL-001 C1; load tests on representative fill at TRL 4

claim: The two battens alone bridge a 0.8 m void under a 100 kg searcher
law: Bending of two 45 x 70 mm battens at mid-span against C16 timber bending strength 16 MPa (EN 338), a factor of 2 required

claim: Four haulers pull the stretcher 15 degrees up debris with 189 N each
law: Coulomb friction mu 0.5 on debris plus the slope term, 100 kg casualty and the 3.9 kg stretcher; sustained pull per hauler 200 N over a short distance

claim: The first probe line starts 4.6 min after the alarm, inside the 300 s of PR-001
law: Sum of legs: run 100 m at 2.5 m/s, open 30 s, carry 100 m at 0.8 m/s, lookout 20 s, boards 60 s; the speeds and opening time are estimates

claim: No flame or smoking near the debris, and stop on any gas smell, removes the ignition sources for landfill gas; with no detector it does not remove toxic or asphyxiant gas (see S29)
law: Methane is explosive in air only between 5 % and 15 % by volume; landfill gas is typically about 50 % methane and 40 to 60 % carbon dioxide, so gas that has migrated and diluted can be in the explosive range (ATSDR Landfill Gas Primer, chapter 3, 2001, checked 2026-11-03). The rule removes ignition sources; it does not detect gas, and carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide can harm without any smell or flame
check: Rule stands; a detector is not added (HPL-DDR-001 item 11); a partner who maintains one would allow it
closed_by: Co-design review at TRL 4; PRC safety section

claim: AA alkaline cells stored out of the lamps stay usable for 12 months in a warm shed
law: Alkaline cells lose charge slowly and can leak when left flat inside equipment; the kit stores them in their packet. No shelf-life figure or temperature limit was checked against a maker's datasheet
check: Maker's shelf life at shed temperature to assess; monthly inspection log

claim: Cut-resistant gloves, boots and glasses make a search on sharp waste acceptable
law: Wounds contaminated with dirt or soil, and puncture wounds, are higher risk for tetanus; vaccination status decides the care needed (CDC, Clinical Guidance for Wound Management to Prevent Tetanus, checked 2026-11-03). PPE lowers the injury rate but does not remove it; the kit gives first-aid wording only, not medical treatment
check: PPE reduces, does not remove, wound and infection risk; vaccination advice goes with the drill card
closed_by: PRC safety section; RSK hazard H6

claim: A six-part tackle turns the pull of six people into 5 kN with under 200 N each
law: Real advantage = sum of k^i for six parts, k = 0.93 per bushed sheave (estimate), 4.69 against the ideal 6; tail pull 1066 N shared by 6 rope handles. First draft with five handles needed 213 N each, above the 200 N sustained; fix (HPL-DDR-006, standing instruction): six handles

claim: The rope grab can hold the tail while the hands let go
law: A cam grab holds if the clamp load N satisfies mu N >= tail tension; mu 0.3 on rope is an estimate (no source checked) and the 6 kN clamp load is an assumed figure to be replaced by the grab maker's rated hold; the same mu is used in S26. Tail tension at 5 kN load
closed_by: Rope grab hold test at TRL 4

claim: The 125 mm sheaves keep the rope's bend ratio at about 8 or more
law: D/d = 125 / 14 (same usual guidance as S9, not checked against a source)
closed_by: Rope supplier's bend-ratio data at TRL 4

claim: Four people at the lever give the 5 kN pull with under 150 N each
law: Pull = handle force x lever ratio x efficiency; ratio 12.2 (1.6 m lever over 131 mm to the drive pin; assumes all four hands at 1.6 m, so a cross handle at the end is to be assessed), efficiency 0.7 (estimate). First draft with a 1.1 m lever needed 213 N each; fix (HPL-DDR-006, standing instruction): lever 1.6 m

claim: Four people sustain 15 strokes a minute of 120 mm
law: Power each = pull x rope speed / efficiency / 4 = 5,000 N x 0.030 m/s / 0.7 / 4

claim: A grooved steel cam grips 14 mm polyester rope at 5 kN without cutting or glazing it
law: Holding 5 kN by friction alone at mu 0.3 (estimate) needs a clamp load of 16.7 kN, about 8.5 MPa over a 14 x 140 mm groove. No rope maker's limit on clamp pressure was checked; polyester fibre melts or glazes under frictional heating and crushes under high clamp load, and the capstan (option A) loads the rope far more gently over four turns
check: Clamp pressure high; rope supplier's limit to assess
closed_by: Grip test on the rope at TRL 4

claim: The capstan wave arrives 14.8 min after the alarm from 500 m, inside the 15 min of PR-015
law: Run to the host shed at 2.5 m/s, 60 s to open the crate, carry back at 0.8 m/s with 21.4 kg each; the 25 kg carry limit and the pace are the 100 m figures applied over 500 m, and the seven people are two waves (four, then three), not four
closed_by: Timed drills at TRL 4 over 500 m; HPL-DDR-004 limit

claim: A 1,000 N knee load on the deck between the battens stays inside the 15 mm plywood's bending strength
law: Bending of a 15 mm plywood strip on the clear span between the battens; the 20 MPa allowed is an unsourced value, a factor of 1.5
closed_by: HPL-CAL-001 C3; plywood maker's data at TRL 4

claim: Dug voids and holes can hold carbon dioxide or hydrogen sulfide that a flame or smell rule does not catch
law: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air and collects in holes and trenches; hydrogen sulfide dulls the sense of smell (ATSDR, Landfill Gas Primer, ch. 3, checked 2026-11-03). Searchers dig where casualties lie, so the no-flame rule (S18) only removes ignition sources
check: Digging guidance added for the drill card: no one goes head first into a hole, a watcher at every hole, back out on headache, dizziness or any smell; the six-signal stop rule is not changed (HPL-DDR-006)
closed_by: Co-design review at TRL 4; RSK hazard H8; Amish asked whether to add a seventh stop signal
